newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore shares up at noon despite profit-taking.
newsitem.headline: Singapore shares up at noon despite profit-taking.

text.p: Singapore shares were broadly firmer at noon Tuesday with several bouts of profit-taking in the morning well absorbed, said dealers.
"The market is off its high because of profit-taking but it is still looking good. Sentiment is generally upbeat because of the coming budget," said a broker with a Singapore brokerage.
Singapore is due to announce its new budget this Friday.
Some funds were picking Singapore stocks in anticipation of an economic recovery in the second half of the year but much of the volume was also generated by day-traders, he said.
The Straits Times Industrial Index was firmer by 10.13 points to 2,008.12. Volume is 118.99 million shares with 202 gainers against 120 losers.
Topping the actives was speculative Van der Horst which gained 23 cents to Singapore $2.58 on volume of 5.84 million units. The company said it won an oil pipeline project in Indonesia.
Singapore Press foreign touched a new high of S$30.70 before settling at S$30.60, up 40 cents.
"It is looking a bit rich at these levels. PE is about 30 times but earnings growth is about 10 percent this year," an analyst with foreign broking firm said.
Singapore Airlines foreign also saw some fund buying and touched a high of S$13.90 before easing to S$13.60, unchanged from its previous close.
